about.title: About this policy
about.description: This privacy policy explains how Aperim Pty Ltd ("we", "us", "our") collects, holds, uses, and discloses personal information in connection with the Production City website at production.city and any related services.
about.obligations: We are bound by the Australian Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) ("Privacy Act") and the Australian Privacy Principles ("APPs"). This policy is intended to satisfy our obligations under APP 1 to manage personal information in an open and transparent way.
about.contact: If you have questions about this policy or how we handle your personal information, contact us at privacy@production.city.

dataCollection.title: Personal information we collect
dataCollection.description: We may collect the following categories of personal information:
items: Identity information — your name and email address, provided when you submit an expression of interest or create an account.
Submission content — the category of interest you select, any optional message you provide, and category-specific information such as a company name or portfolio URL.
Contact information — your phone number in E.164 format, if you choose to subscribe to SMS notifications.
Technical information — your IP address, browser type and version, referring page URL, and UTM campaign parameters, collected automatically when you visit the site.
Consent records — the version of this privacy policy you accepted, the timestamp of acceptance, and your marketing communication preference.
Session information — a hashed session token, your IP address, and user agent string, collected when you log in.
Audit information — records of actions you take within the platform, including the action type, timestamp, IP address, and user agent, stored for security and compliance purposes.
dataCollection.sensitive: We do not collect sensitive information as defined in the Privacy Act (such as health information, racial or ethnic origin, or political opinions) unless you voluntarily include it in a free-text message field.

howWeCollect.title: How we collect personal information
items: directly from you, when you submit an expression of interest, create an account, subscribe to notifications, or contact us;
automatically, through server logs and the Cloudflare Web Analytics service when you visit our website; and
from third-party services, such as Postmark delivery status notifications and Twilio SMS status callbacks.
howWeCollect.note: Where reasonably practicable, we collect personal information directly from you. We do not purchase personal information from third-party data brokers.

purpose.title: Why we collect, use, and disclose your information
purpose.description: We collect, use, and disclose your personal information for the following purposes:
items: to respond to your expression of interest and communicate with you about Production City;
to send you a confirmation email acknowledging your submission;
to send marketing communications, only where you have given explicit opt-in consent;
to send SMS notifications about categories you have subscribed to, only with your confirmed consent;
to authenticate your identity and maintain your session when you log in;
to analyse submission trends and website usage to improve our services;
to maintain audit logs for security, fraud prevention, and regulatory compliance;
to manage email and SMS suppression lists to honour your unsubscribe requests and comply with the Spam Act 2003 (Cth) and the Do Not Call Register Act 2006 (Cth);
to comply with applicable laws, regulations, and legal processes.
purpose.note: We will not use or disclose your personal information for a purpose other than the purpose of collection, a related purpose you would reasonably expect, or a purpose to which you have consented, unless required or authorised by law (APP 6).

lawfulBasis.title: Australian Privacy Principles
lawfulBasis.consent: APP 6 — Use and disclosure: We use and disclose personal information only for the primary purpose of collection, a directly related secondary purpose, or where you have consented.
lawfulBasis.legitimateInterest: APP 7 — Direct marketing: We send marketing communications only with your explicit opt-in consent. You may withdraw consent at any time by unsubscribing.
lawfulBasis.marketing: APP 11 — Security: We take reasonable steps to protect personal information from misuse, interference, loss, and unauthorised access, modification, or disclosure.

marketing.title: Direct marketing
marketing.description: We will only send you marketing communications (by email or SMS) if you have explicitly opted in (APP 7). You can withdraw your consent and unsubscribe at any time by:
items: clicking the unsubscribe link in any marketing email;
replying STOP to any SMS message;
contacting us at privacy@production.city.
marketing.spam: We will process your unsubscribe request promptly. Every marketing email includes a working unsubscribe mechanism as required by the Spam Act 2003.

thirdParties.title: Disclosure to third parties
thirdParties.description: We share personal information with the following service providers who process data on our behalf under contractual data processing obligations.
thirdParties.note: No additional third-party services receive personal information beyond those listed above. We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information to third parties for their own marketing purposes.

crossBorder.title: Cross-border disclosure
crossBorder.description: Your personal information may be disclosed to service providers located in the United States. Before disclosing personal information to an overseas recipient, we take reasonable steps to ensure the recipient does not breach the APPs in relation to that information, or we rely on an exception under APP 8.2 (such as your informed consent or a binding contractual arrangement that requires the recipient to handle information consistently with the APPs).
countries: United States — Cloudflare (hosting, analytics), Postmark (email), Twilio (SMS), Google (font delivery)
crossBorder.note: No other countries. All third-party data processing occurs in the United States as listed above.

security.title: Data quality and security
security.description: We take reasonable steps to ensure the personal information we collect, use, and disclose is accurate, up-to-date, complete, and relevant (APP 10), and to protect personal information from misuse, interference, loss, and unauthorised access, modification, or disclosure (APP 11). Our security measures include:
items: encryption in transit (TLS/HTTPS on all connections);
hashing of session tokens using SHA-256 before storage;
hashing of magic link tokens and verification codes before storage;
HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite cookie attributes on authentication cookies;
Content Security Policy headers restricting script and resource loading;
automated session cleanup after 30 days of inactivity;
automatic expiry of magic links (15 minutes for login, 7 days for invitations);
email and SMS suppression lists to prevent delivery to addresses that have bounced or reported spam;
audit logging of significant account actions.
security.note: We review our security practices periodically. No system is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security of your information.

retention.title: Data retention
retention.description: We retain personal information for as long as necessary for the purposes described in this policy, subject to any legal obligations that require longer retention. You may request earlier deletion of your personal information at any time (see the accessing and correcting section below).

cookiesSection.title: Cookies and tracking technologies
cookiesSection.description: Our website uses cookies and local storage to support authentication and language preferences. We use Cloudflare Web Analytics for traffic analysis — this service does not use cookies and does not collect personal information.
cookiesSection.analytics: We do not use any other third-party tracking cookies, advertising cookies, or cross-site tracking technologies.
cookiesSection.link: For full details, see our Cookie Policy.

children.title: Children's privacy
children.description: Our website and services are not directed at children under the age of 16. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 16. If we become aware that we have collected personal information from a child under 16 without parental consent, we will take reasonable steps to delete that information promptly.
children.contact: If you are a parent or guardian and believe your child has provided us with personal information, please contact us at privacy@production.city.

anonymity.title: Anonymity and pseudonymity
anonymity.description: Where it is lawful and practicable, you may deal with us without identifying yourself or by using a pseudonym (APP 2). However, if you do not provide the personal information we request, we may not be able to respond to your expression of interest or provide you with access to certain features.

rights.title: Accessing and correcting your personal information
rights.description: Under APPs 12 and 13, you have the right to:
items: request access to the personal information we hold about you;
request correction of any information that is inaccurate, out-of-date, incomplete, irrelevant, or misleading;
request deletion of your personal information (subject to any legal obligations that require us to retain it).
rights.contact: To exercise these rights, contact us at privacy@production.city. We will respond to your request within 30 days. We will not charge you for making a request, but we may charge a reasonable fee for providing access if your request requires substantial effort to fulfil.
rights.note: If we refuse to provide access or correct information, we will give you written reasons and inform you of the complaint mechanisms available to you.

ndb.title: Notifiable data breaches
ndb.description: If we become aware of a data breach that is likely to result in serious harm to any individual whose personal information is involved, we will:
items: take reasonable steps to contain the breach and mitigate harm;
assess the breach to determine whether it is an eligible data breach under Part IIIC of the Privacy Act;
if the breach is eligible, notify the affected individuals and the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) as soon as practicable;
keep a record of the breach regardless of whether notification is required.

complaints.title: Complaints
complaints.description: If you believe we have breached the APPs or handled your personal information improperly, you may lodge a complaint by contacting us at privacy@production.city. We will:
steps: investigate the complaint and provide a response within 30 days;
take reasonable steps to resolve the matter.

oaic.description: If you are not satisfied with our response, you may lodge a complaint with the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC):

jurisdiction.title: Governing Law
jurisdiction.description: This privacy policy is governed by the laws of New South Wales, Australia, and the Australian Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and the Australian Privacy Principles.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.description: We may update this privacy policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices, services, or applicable law. When we make material changes, we will update the effective date at the top of this page. The consent version recorded with your submission refers to the version of this policy you accepted.

whatAreCookies.title: What are cookies
whatAreCookies.description: Cookies are small text files placed on your device by a website. They are widely used to make websites work efficiently and to provide information to website operators. Cookies can be "session" cookies (deleted when you close your browser) or "persistent" cookies (retained on your device until they expire or you delete them).
whatAreCookies.localStorage: Local storage is a browser feature that allows websites to store data on your device. Unlike cookies, local storage data is not sent to the server with each request.

cookiesWeUse.title: Cookies we use
cookiesWeUse.description: We use a small number of cookies, all of which are functional. We do not use advertising, tracking, or analytics cookies.
cookiesWeUse.essentialDescription: These cookies are necessary for the Website to function. You cannot opt out of essential cookies because the Website would not work without them.
cookiesWeUse.functionalDescription: These cookies improve your experience by remembering your preferences. They are not required for the Website to function but provide useful features.

localStorage.title: Local storage
localStorage.description: We use browser local storage to remember your language preference.
localStorage.note: Local storage data stays on your device and is not transmitted to our servers with each page request.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.description: We use Cloudflare Web Analytics for aggregated website traffic analysis. This service does not use cookies, does not collect personal information, does not track individual visitors across websites, and processes anonymised, aggregated traffic data only.
analytics.note: Cloudflare Web Analytics is loaded via a script from static.cloudflareinsights.com and operates in a way that preserves visitor privacy.

thirdParty.title: Third-party cookies and external resources
thirdParty.description: We do not embed third-party cookies on the Website. We do not use social media plugins, advertising trackers, or third-party analytics services that set cookies.
thirdParty.fonts: Our Website loads web font files (Noto Sans for Arabic, Devanagari, and Bengali script support) directly from Google's font delivery network at fonts.gstatic.com. Google does not set cookies through this font delivery mechanism. However, when your browser requests font files, Google receives your IP address and browser user-agent string. Google's handling of this data is governed by Google's Privacy Policy at policies.google.com/privacy.
thirdParty.analytics: The only other third-party domain from which scripts are loaded is static.cloudflareinsights.com (Cloudflare Web Analytics), which does not set cookies.

managing.title: Managing cookies and local storage
managing.description: You can manage cookies through your browser settings. Most browsers allow you to view what cookies are set, delete individual or all cookies, block cookies from specific or all websites, and block third-party cookies.
managing.browsers: Instructions for managing cookies in common browsers:
browserList: Chrome: Settings, then Privacy and Security, then Cookies and other site data
Firefox: Settings, then Privacy and Security, then Cookies and Site Data
Safari: Preferences, then Privacy, then Manage Website Data
Edge: Settings, then Cookies and site permissions, then Manage and delete cookies and site data
managing.sessionNote: If you block essential cookies (__Secure-session), you will not be able to log in or maintain an authenticated session on the Website.
managing.localStorageNote: To clear local storage data, use your browser's developer tools or clear all site data through your browser's privacy settings. If you clear the pc-locale local storage item, the Website will default to English and will not remember your language preference between visits.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.description: We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time to reflect changes in the cookies we use or for other operational, legal, or regulatory reasons. When we make changes, we will update the effective date at the top of this page.

meta.title: Production City — We Make Stories
meta.description: Production City fuses tradition and innovation for screen, stage, and experiential storytelling. Register your interest today.

intro.positioning: A vertically integrated studio campus. Sound stages, LED volume, broadcast theatre, and the full service stack — built as one system, not assembled from vendors.

whatIs.heading: What is Production City?
whatIs.claim1: One operator running the venue, the technology, and the full creative service stack.
whatIs.claim2: Sound stages, broadcast theatre, LED volume, and the full service stack — on one campus.
whatIs.claim3: Building a global campus network, beginning in Sydney.
whatIs.claim4: Modern infrastructure built on established production craft, not the other way around.

creativePreview.heading: An Integrated Creative Ecosystem
creativePreview.description: Seventeen disciplines. One campus. One operator. Pre-production through post — no vendor handoffs.

visionTeaser.heading: A Global Vision
visionTeaser.description: Sydney is the first campus. Switzerland, Singapore, Africa, and the United States follow — one operator, one standard, replicated city by city.

eoi.heading: Stay Informed
eoi.context: Register your interest to stay informed about Production City's progress.

communityPreview.heading: Community & Sustainability
communityPreview.description: Education, skills, and community work embedded in the campus — not announced when the project needs goodwill.

masterplanTeaser.heading: The campus, in three dimensions.
masterplanTeaser.body: Six sound stages, a broadcast theatre, creative hub, backlot, and public realm — explore the full 6-hectare site as an interactive 3D model.

hero.heading: We make stories.
hero.subtitle: A vertically integrated studio campus. Sound stages, LED volume, a broadcast theatre, and the full service stack — built together, in one place.

operatingModel.heading: One operator. One campus. Script to delivery.
operatingModel.body1: Production City is not a stage with vendors bolted on. It is one operator providing the venue, the technology stack, and the full creative service stack under one brand. That reduces coordination risk for tenants and opens multiple revenue streams for the company.
operatingModel.body2: The stages, the LED volume, the broadcast theatre, the control room, and the service teams were designed together. Not retrofitted.

realtime.title: One IP · two formats
realtime.text: Script, libretto, score, pre-vis and digital assets are authored once, then split into a screen lane and a stage lane that run in parallel rather than in sequence.

oneOperator.title: One operator · one campus
oneOperator.text: Venue, stack and service teams under a single brand. Tenants sign one contract, coordinate with one counterparty, and draw on whichever combination of capabilities the work requires.

screenStages.name: Screen Sound Stages
screenStages.description: Large-format sound stages designed for grand-scale productions with configurable LED volume environments.

detail.heading: Grand-scale screen work. Engineered for it.
detail.lead: 2,025 m² of stage floor. 15 m to grid. NRC 1.05. Full-surround LED volume ready.
detail.prose: Feature film. Episodic. Live television. When the production is large-format, the stage has to be built for it from the ground up.
detail.prose2: Each screen sound stage is 45 m × 45 m, 15 m to grid, full-coverage grid and catwalk. Sound-proofing is NRC 1.05 / NC 25. LED volume is configurable flat, arc, or full-surround.
detail.prose3: These stages were designed against the technical specifications of major-studio and streamer productions. As the first site, the standards are set here.

commercialStages.name: Commercial Sound Stages
commercialStages.description: Compact sound stages for commercials, TVCs, music videos, and other smaller-scale content, with configurable LED environments.

detail.heading: Small footprint. Full specification.
detail.lead: 100 m² of stage. Same 15 m to grid. Same sound-proofing. Walk-in-ready LED volume.
detail.prose: Commercials, TVCs, music videos, short-form, and digital work do not need the 45 × 45. They do need proper acoustics, proper height, and the same LED configurations.
detail.prose2: That is what these stages are. Walk in on a Monday. Shoot. Strike by Friday. The volume configurations are shared with the screen stages, so a look developed on one can move to the other.

broadcastTheatre.name: Broadcast Theatre
broadcastTheatre.description: A multi-purpose venue planned for live performance, live broadcast, and VR/AR showcase. Audience-facing and camera-facing in the same space.

detail.heading: A live theatre wired as a broadcast studio.
detail.lead: 450 in theatre mode. 300 in cabaret. Eight fully integrated robotic camera positions. AR and VR ready. Broadcast-partner compliant.
detail.prose: The broadcast theatre is a multi-modal live venue with a broadcast gallery wrapped around it.
detail.prose2: Robotic cameras, an LED virtual set library, and streaming compliance are built into the room. Every performance here can reach the people in the seats and the audience at home at the same time, without a separate broadcast setup.
detail.cta: Discuss a live broadcast or event.

controlRoom.name: Broadcast Control Room
controlRoom.description: Planned central command post for live production coordination, synchronisation, and multi-platform broadcasting.

detail.heading: The nerve centre.
detail.lead: Central production management, live broadcast control, advanced synchronisation — feeding stages, the theatre, and external venues globally.
detail.prose: The control room is the campus’s single broadcast spine. It manages and synchronises every live production on site.
detail.prose2: It is designed to originate broadcast from external sports and event venues anywhere in the world. Production City’s broadcast and data-centre pedigree sits here. The control room is engineered the way critical broadcast infrastructure is engineered.
detail.cap3: Advanced synchronisation across multi-platform and multi-location broadcasts
detail.cap4: Origination from on-campus stages and theatre
detail.cap5: Origination from external sports and event venues globally

ecosystem.principle1: Physical and digital workflows are the same workflow.
ecosystem.principle2: Departments run concurrently. Props and post overlap. Shooting and script development overlap.
ecosystem.principle3: Workshop, stage, and edit suite sit on the same site. No logistics chain.
ecosystem.principle4: Problems get solved in real time because the people who can solve them are in the building.
ecosystem.principle5: One operator means one set of decisions. Less friction for tenants. Cleaner revenue for the company.
ecosystem.benefit2: A prop built in the workshop reaches the stage without leaving the campus.
ecosystem.benefit3: A take finished in the gallery is graded a floor away.
ecosystem.benefit4: Efficiency is structural — it doesn't need to be managed onto it.
ecosystem.benefit5: Cost comes out of logistics, not production quality.
ecosystem.benefit6: Risk sits with us, not the production.

mission.heading: Vision & Mission
mission.vision: Production City builds the physical, technical, and cultural infrastructure that storytelling at scale requires — campus by campus, in the cities where that work happens.
mission.theme2: Put LED volume, VR/AR, and live broadcast into the daily production pipeline
mission.theme3: Run the campus as one integrated system, not a collection of vendors
mission.theme4: Build knowledge and research into the campus — not alongside it
mission.theme5: Open serious production infrastructure to more creators
mission.theme6: Tell stories from more places and more cultures
mission.theme7: Operate in a way that earns the campus its place in the community
mission.phil1: Technology serves the story. It doesn't replace the craft.
mission.phil2: Vertical integration exists to reduce risk, not to build empire.
mission.phil3: Innovation earns its place when it works reliably on a live set.
mission.phil4: A campus that serves one kind of storyteller has already narrowed its value.

global.heading: Global Campus Network
global.operatingModel: Each campus runs under the same brand, the same technology stack, and the same ownership model. A production that starts in Sydney can continue in Singapore on the same terms.
global.sydneyDesc: First campus. Technical standards, R&D, and executive functions are set here before replication.
global.singaporeDesc: Preferred Asia-Pacific site. Assessment in progress, chosen for production demand, regional connectivity, and incentive structure.
global.hawaiiDesc: Pacific bridge campus. Connects Asia-Pacific and North American production schedules across time zones.
global.europeDesc: Switzerland is the current leading candidate, chosen for neutrality, multilingual workforce, and proximity to European broadcast demand.
global.usaDesc: Committed once the first international campuses are operational. Site selection follows, not the other way around.

meta.title: FAQ — Production City
meta.description: Frequently asked questions about Production City's facilities, services, global network, and community engagement.

faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What types of facilities will Production City offer?
faq.a1: Production City plans to offer Screen Sound Stages, Commercial Sound Stages, a Broadcast Control Room, a multi-functional Broadcast Theatre, and spaces for research & development and educational collaborations.
faq.q2: Will Production City's services be available for international locations?
faq.a2: Yes. Production City plans to expand to Singapore, Hawaii, Europe, and mainland USA with consistent facilities and services across all campuses.
faq.q3: What virtual production services will Production City provide?
faq.a3: Pre-vis, shooting, post, VFX, motion capture, CGI, and VR/AR on one campus under one operator. No hand-offs between separate vendors.
faq.q4: How will Production City support educational initiatives?
faq.a4: The campus includes an education programme built into operations. Students learn on working stages and in active post suites, not in a classroom annex.
faq.q5: What research and development facilities will Production City include?
faq.a5: R&D sits inside the production operation, not alongside it. The team tests new tools, workflows, and formats against real productions on the same campus.
faq.q6: What kinds of projects will be suitable for Production City?
faq.a6: Feature films, TV series, live telecasts, stage productions, music videos, VR/AR content, and other forms of content creation.
faq.a7: One campus. One operator. The craft and the technology in the same building, under the same management — not coordinated between separate vendors.
faq.q8: What kind of support services will Production City offer for a smooth production process?
faq.a8: End-to-end virtual production, pre-production, filming, post-production, VFX, sound mixing, dressing rooms, catering, on-site set and prop construction, and digitisation services.
faq.q9: What will make Production City's sound stages unique?
faq.a9: 15 m height to grid, NRC 1.05 acoustic isolation, and LED volume configurations sized for different production scales.
faq.q10: How will Production City's services simplify the production workflow?
faq.a10: By co-locating pre-production, production, and post-production services on one campus to reduce transport, coordination, and scheduling complexity.
faq.q11: What benefits will the LED volume offer for productions?
faq.a11: Flexible configurations, real-time visual effects, efficient background changes, and a cost/time-effective alternative to traditional green screen methods.
faq.q12: How will Production City commit to sustainability efforts?
faq.a12: Sustainability is designed into the campus plan. Energy systems, waste management, green spaces, and biodiversity targets are part of the site design, not added after construction.
faq.q13: Will the Production City facilities accommodate pre-production and post-production processes?
faq.a13: Yes. Script development, storyboarding, concept design, editing, sound mixing, colour grading, and visual effects will all be part of the planned offering.
faq.q14: How will being a part of the Production City network enrich a creative professional's experience?
faq.a14: Access to sound stages, LED volume, post-production, and broadcast, plus the people working in them. The campus runs workshops and collaborative programmes, and the global network connects creators across sites.
faq.q15: Will clients be able to provide their own technical crew, or will Production City supply them?
faq.a15: Both options are planned. Clients will be able to bring their own crew, and Production City will also be able to provide technical support personnel.
faq.q16: How can clients stay updated with the latest developments or offerings at Production City?
faq.a16: By registering interest on the website, subscribing to the newsletter, or following Production City's social media channels.
faq.q17: How will Production City foster talent growth and innovation?
faq.a17: By partnering with educational institutions, offering hands-on learning, maintaining R&D facilities, and running workshops and skill development programs.
faq.q18: What measures will Production City have to ensure safety and security?
faq.a18: Security personnel, surveillance, secure access controls, fire safety systems, and health and safety protocols aligned with industry standards.
faq.q19: How will Production City cater to different scale productions — from independent creators to corporate entities?
faq.a19: By offering facilities planned for all scales of production and the same level of professional support regardless of project size.
faq.q20: What kinds of engagements beyond facility rentals will be possible?
faq.a20: Technology partnerships, education and research collaborations, joint development of filming methods and techniques, and collaborative business models.

meta.title: First Nations approach — Production City
meta.description: Governance, IP and data practice, workforce, community work, and the stories this campus is built to serve are shaped by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander ways of Knowing, Being, and Doing.

firstNations.heading: Embedded, not added on.
firstNations.lead: Our governance, our intellectual property and data practice, our workforce, our community work, and the stories this campus is built to serve are shaped by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander ways of Knowing, Being, and Doing.
firstNations.ackQuote: Production City acknowledges the Traditional Owners of Country throughout Australia, and the Traditional Custodians of the lands on which a Sydney campus would be built. We pay our respects to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Elders past and present. We acknowledge that sovereignty was never ceded, and that storytelling on these lands is among the oldest continuous creative practice anywhere in the world.
firstNations.leadershipBio1: Matthew Compton is Chief Operating Officer and Managing Director. He leads operational delivery across the business. His role in the organisation is a principal reason this approach is implemented rather than spoken about.
firstNations.leadershipBio2: Matthew holds an MBA (Leadership and Enterprise) from the University of Sydney, a Bachelor of Business Management from the University of Queensland, and is a Member of the Australian Institute of Company Directors. He is a sessional academic at the University of Sydney and an Associate Lecturer at Western Sydney University, where he teaches innovation and business leadership and contributes to the WSU Indigenous Centre of Excellence.
firstNations.leadershipBio3: He sits on the University of Sydney Faculty of Medicine and Health First Nations Cultural Safety Advisory Group.
firstNations.ip1: Free, prior, and informed consent is embedded in how we handle material from or referencing First Nations communities.
firstNations.ip2: Provenance is tracked end-to-end. The origin of training data, reference material, captured performance, and derived assets is recorded and auditable.
firstNations.ip3: Cultural safety protocols are built into production workflows, including virtual production, motion capture, and generative tools.
firstNations.ip4: Benefit remains with the people a story comes from — agreements keep recognition and benefit with communities, not the production company by default.
firstNations.onCountryHeading: Education, skills, and community — delivered on Country.
firstNations.onCountryDesc: Our education and skills work is designed to be delivered on Country, with Traditional Owners and community organisations, rather than only at the campus gate. The campus is a hub. The programme extends outward.
firstNations.onCountry1: Entry pathways into screen, broadcast, and virtual production, with mentoring and paid placements.
firstNations.onCountry3: Long-horizon capability building into durable, high-skill roles.
firstNations.onCountry4: Procurement pathways for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander owned businesses across construction, operations, and creative supply.
firstNations.creativeHeading: Country, at production scale. Audiences, on terms communities control.
firstNations.creativeDesc: Virtual production and LED volumes make it possible to render Country at production scale without disturbing it. Live broadcast, AR, and VR open new paths to audiences. The campus is built to help First Nations storytellers reach national and international audiences on terms they control.
firstNations.evidence1: Board and executive governance arrangements, including the COO’s portfolio and decision rights.
firstNations.evidence2: IP and data provenance framework, including protocols for First Nations material.
firstNations.evidence3: Targets and reporting commitments for employment, procurement, and training.
firstNations.evidence4: Partnership and community relationships through which the programme is delivered.

meta.title: The company — Production City
meta.description: Production City is an Australian company that designs, builds, and operates vertically integrated content production campuses. Sydney is the first site, not a branch.

company.heading: A first site, not a branch.
company.lead: Production City is an Australian company that designs, builds, and operates vertically integrated content production campuses across five continents — Australia, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, and North America.
company.what1: Production City combines established production craft with modern technology inside a single vertically integrated campus. The technology stack includes virtual production, LED volumes, motion capture, AR and VR, and connected broadcast — all designed together, not retrofitted.
company.what2: We operate the venue, the technology, and the services ourselves, under one brand. That reduces coordination risk for tenants and opens multiple revenue streams for the company.
company.what3: Our international footprint spans five continents — Australia, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, and North America. Each campus is built to the same technical specification, under the same operator and brand.
company.pillar1Desc: One operator. One campus. Venue, technology stack, and full creative services — from script to delivery — under one brand.
company.pillar2Title: A First Nations approach, embedded throughout
company.pillar2Desc: Governance, intellectual property and data practice, workforce, and the stories this campus is built to serve — shaped by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander ways of Knowing, Being, and Doing.
company.pillar3Desc: Broadcast and data-centre pedigree informs how the company engineers. Uptime, safety, and operational reliability come from that discipline.
company.pillar4Desc: Five continents — Australia, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, and North America. One operator, one standard, replicated campus by campus.
company.pillar5Desc: Sustainable design principles, energy and waste performance, biodiversity on the campus plan, and community dialogue that is ongoing rather than commissioning-phase.
company.leadershipNote: The wider executive team brings senior experience in screen education, animation and visual effects, virtual production and broadcast technology, music rights and US partnerships, and industry engagement. Full bios for each executive and non-executive director are provided on request.
company.partnersIntro: Production City is in advanced engagement across four partner categories. Named partners and the nature of each arrangement are disclosed where commercial confidentiality allows.
company.partner1Desc: Tertiary and training partners to establish a talent pipeline and skills development programme from campus opening. Specific pathways are co-designed with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander education providers and community organisations.
company.partner2Desc: Major providers in virtual production, LED volume, real-time rendering, broadcast, and connected production. The technology stack is set at the first site and replicated across the network.
company.partner3Desc: Capital and research partners co-investing in innovation capability embedded in the campus, rather than adjacent to it. Research is treated as infrastructure, not overhead.
company.partner4Desc: First Nations owned businesses, community organisations, and Traditional Owner groups whose involvement shapes the workforce, procurement, cultural safety, and creative work of the campus.
company.partnersNote: Named partners are disclosed where commercial confidentiality allows. Early-stage engagements remain under commercial terms until agreements are signed.
company.pullQuote: The first campus is being built now. Technical standards, research and development, and the executive functions of the network are based at that first site. Being first is not a branding claim — it is a structural one, and it compounds.
company.leadershipBio1: Founder and Chief Executive. Stage and screen production, broadcast and data-centre infrastructure, machine learning in Silicon Valley.
company.leadershipBio2: Chief Operating Officer and Managing Director. His authority is substantive, not advisory.

companyTeam.troyBio1: Troy began in stage and screen, touring theatrical productions internationally and working across live performance before moving into institutional production. He served as Chief Technology Officer at the Australian Film, Television and Radio School (AFTRS), where his portfolio covered the technology backbone of a national screen institution.
companyTeam.troyBio2: After AFTRS he led the delivery of broadcast and data-centre infrastructure in Australia — projects engineered to the standards that critical infrastructure demands. In the United States he worked in machine learning in Silicon Valley, applying engineering discipline to production-grade AI systems.
companyTeam.troyBio3: He founded Production City™ to combine those three threads — production craft, broadcast engineering, and modern computing — into a single operator.
companyTeam.matthewRole: Chief Operating Officer · Managing Director · Wiradjuri
companyTeam.matthewBio1: Matthew is Chief Operating Officer and Managing Director. He leads operational delivery across the business. His role is substantive, not advisory — a principal reason the First Nations approach is implemented rather than spoken about.
companyTeam.matthewBio2: He holds an MBA (Leadership and Enterprise) from the University of Sydney, a Bachelor of Business Management from the University of Queensland, and is a Member of the Australian Institute of Company Directors.
companyTeam.matthewBio3: Matthew is a sessional academic at the University of Sydney and an Associate Lecturer at Western Sydney University, where he teaches innovation and business leadership and contributes to the WSU Indigenous Centre of Excellence. He sits on the University of Sydney Faculty of Medicine and Health First Nations Cultural Safety Advisory Group.

meta.title: Approach — Production City
meta.description: The operating model, in one page.

companyApproach.heading: Built together. Not retrofitted.
companyApproach.lead: The operating model, in one page.
companyApproach.vert1: The traditional studio model coordinates many vendors across many sites. That works, but it moves the risk and the cost onto the production.
companyApproach.vert2: Production City operates the venue, the technology, and the full creative service stack ourselves, under one brand. Coordination risk sits with us. Revenue streams are diversified across facilities, services, and broadcast — which is part of why this model is bankable at the scale of a campus.
companyApproach.vert3: This is also why we can make commitments to tenants about pipeline time. A set built in our workshop does not leave the campus to reach the stage. A take finished in the gallery is graded a floor away. A live performance is broadcast from the control room without a second production being stood up around it.
companyApproach.vert4: The argument is simple. The execution is not. The team that engineered the campus came to it from broadcast, from data-centre infrastructure, and from production craft — which is closer to the actual demand than a pure property development approach.
companyApproach.platformDesc: A complex production and site management system is in design. It will handle scheduling, crew, tenants, billing, and broadcast orchestration at campus scale. That system is operator-facing, not public. This website will link to tenant and partner portals when they exist.

circulation.pedestrianDesc: Internal walkways connect stage lobbies, offices, and support facilities without crossing vehicle routes.
